title: Portuguese reach the Gabon estuary
description: Portuguese sailors chart the estuary, and their word 'gabão', a hooded cloak, in time names the whole country.

title: France signs treaties with coastal chiefs
description: Captain Bouët-Willaumez gets King Denis Rapontchombo and other Mpongwe chiefs to sign away sovereignty over their anchorages.

title: Libreville founded
description: Freed slaves taken from a captured Brazilian ship are settled beside Fort d'Aumale, and their town, 'Freetown' in French, becomes the capital.

title: De Brazza explores the Ogooué
description: Pierre Savorgnan de Brazza sets off up the Ogooué, the first of the journeys that open the equatorial interior to France.

title: Franceville founded
description: De Brazza's second expedition plants a post at Masuku on the upper Ogooué, its people drawn from freed slaves.

title: Schweitzer's hospital at Lambaréné
description: Albert Schweitzer, theologian and musician turned doctor, opens the jungle hospital that becomes his life and wins him the Nobel Peace Prize.

title: Battle of Gabon
description: Free French troops under Leclerc and Koenig storm Libreville, the last Vichy holdout in Equatorial Africa.

title: Autonomous republic within the Community
description: After voting for de Gaulle's Community, Gabon governs itself with Léon M'ba as prime minister.

title: Independence from France
description: Gabon becomes independent with Léon M'ba as its first president.

title: Coup attempt and French intervention
description: Officers depose M'ba for two days until French paratroopers fly in and put him back, bloodlessly for France but not for Gabon.

title: Omar Bongo becomes president
description: M'ba dies in office and his deputy Albert-Bernard Bongo succeeds, beginning one of the longest presidencies in the world.

title: One-party state
description: Bongo dissolves every party but his own Gabonese Democratic Party, which runs the country for the next two decades.

title: Trans-Gabon Railway completed
description: The line from Libreville through deep forest reaches Franceville, opening the manganese and timber of the interior to export.

title: Multiparty protests
description: Riots after an opposition figure's suspicious death force Bongo to legalise rival parties, though his own keeps winning elections.

title: Omar Bongo dies
description: The president dies in a Spanish clinic after nearly 42 years in power, leaving the state to his son.

title: Ali Bongo elected
description: Ali Bongo is declared winner of the presidential election; Port-Gentil riots against what it calls a succession.

title: Disputed re-election
description: Bongo is re-elected over Jean Ping by a suspiciously high tally in his home province, and crowds burn the national assembly.

title: Coup attempt fails
description: Junior officers seize the radio station while the president convalesces abroad and are arrested within hours.
